title: Little Office of the Dead
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, Rex gloriae, libera animas omnium fidelium defunctorum de poenis inferni, et de profundo lacu: libera eas de ore leonis, ne absorbeat eas tartarus, ne cadant in obscurum; sed signifer sanctus Michael repraesentet eas in lucem sanctam, quam olim Abrahae promisisti, et semini ejus.
blocks.english: O Lord Jesus Christ, King of glory, deliver the souls of all the faithful departed from the pains of hell and from the deep pit; deliver them from the lion’s mouth, lest the abyss swallow them and they fall into darkness; but may Saint Michael, the standard-bearer, present them into the holy light which Thou didst promise of old to Abraham and his descendants.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: O vos, fideles animae In Christo defunctorum, Sed merito prohibita Ab aditu coelorum:
blocks.english: O faithful souls of those who have died in Christ, yet justly barred from entering heaven,

blocks.source: Quam velim vobis dexteram, Opemque praesentare! Uthine ad caeli gloriam Possitis evolare!
blocks.english: How I wish to offer you my hand and help, that from here you may fly to the glory of heaven!

blocks.source: Ant. Illuminare his, qui in tenebris et in umbra mortis sedent, ad dirigendos pedes eorum in viam pacis.
blocks.english: Ant. To give light to those who sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, to guide their feet into the way of peace.

blocks.source: ℣. Si iniquitates observaveris, Domine,
blocks.english: ℣. If Thou shouldst mark iniquities, O Lord,

blocks.source: ℟. Domine, quis sustinebit?
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, who could endure?

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Fidelium Deus omnium Conditor et Redemptor, animabus famularum famulorumque tuarum remissionem cunctorum tribue peccatorum: ut indulgentiam quam semper optaverunt, piis supplicationibus consequantur. Qui vivis et regnas in saecula saeculorum.
blocks.english: O God, Creator and Redeemer of all the faithful, grant to the souls of Thy servants, women and men, remission of all sins, that through loving supplications they may obtain the pardon they have always desired. Who livest and reignest for ever and ever.
blocks.editorialNote: The visually checked cited 1879 Coeleste Palmetum, p.264, prints the servants in the order “famulorum famularumque tuarum”; the attached PDF reverses the two nouns. English retains both men and women as Thy servants. The printed possessive ending remains unchanged.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Requiem aeternam dona eis, Domine.
blocks.english: ℣. Grant them eternal rest, O Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Et lux perpetua luceat eis.
blocks.english: ℟. And let perpetual light shine upon them.

blocks.source: O magne Pater, nomine Misericordiarum, Facturas tuas respice, Sed timorem remorum: Poenas sunt quidem merita, Te tamen non negabam; Hinc locus sit clementiae: Ignosce, quod peccaram.
blocks.english: O great Father, named Father of mercies, look upon Thy creatures, but forget Thine anger. They have indeed deserved punishment, yet they did not deny Thee. Therefore let there be room for mercy; forgive their sins.
blocks.editorialNote: The cited 1879 edition, p.264, visibly prints “Sed immemor irarum” and plural verbs “negarunt ... peccarunt”, rather than the attached “Sed timorem remorum ... negabam ... peccaram”. The English follows the verified edition, addressing God on behalf of the souls; it replaces the former untranslated line and first-person conjecture. Attached Latin is preserved.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O great Father, named Father of mercies, look upon Thy creatures. [Unclear printed line: “Sed timorem remorum.”] I have indeed deserved punishment, yet I did not deny Thee. Therefore let there be room for mercy; forgive the sins I committed.

blocks.source: O Jesu clementissime, O optime Salvator, Tuo redemptis sanguine Sis mitis liberator.
blocks.english: O most merciful Jesus, O best of Saviours, be a gentle deliverer to those redeemed by Thy blood.

blocks.source: Indulge te amantibus Tuum benignitatem, Poenamque deprecantibus Ostende bonitatem.
blocks.english: Grant Thy kindness to those who love Thee; show Thy goodness to those who implore release from punishment.

blocks.source: O consolator optime, O dulcis Paraclete, Hos tu deserto respice, Et indignos quaerite
blocks.english: O best of comforters, O sweet Paraclete, look upon these abandoned souls, unworthy of rest,
blocks.editorialNote: The cited 1879 edition, p.265, visibly prints “desertos” (abandoned) and “quiete” (rest), corresponding to the attached “deserto” and “quaerite”. “Et indignos quiete” continues the description of the souls; it is not an imperative to seek them. The following stanza supplies the petition “dona” (grant). English follows the checked reading; attached Latin remains.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O best of comforters, O sweet Paraclete, look upon these abandoned souls, and seek out the unworthy,

blocks.source: In aestu hoc temperiem, Veraeque pacis bona, Et post laborem requiem Aeternam his dona.
blocks.english: Grant them relief amid this heat, the blessings of true peace, and after labour give them eternal rest.

blocks.source: O dulcis mater gratiae, Solatrix afflictorum, Vim cohibe justitiae, Rigorem tormentorum.
blocks.english: O sweet Mother of grace, comforter of the afflicted, restrain the force of justice and the severity of torments.

blocks.source: Flammam voracem tempera, Et mitiga dolores, Incendium refrigera, Et fini hos angores.
blocks.english: Temper the devouring flame and soothe their pains; cool the burning fire and end these anguish-filled trials.

blocks.source: Vos, tutelaris genii, Quorum sunt hi clientes, Quantum vestra subsidii Sunt ipsis indigentes!
blocks.english: O guardian spirits, whose clients these are, how greatly they stand in need of your aid!

blocks.source: Plorem desideria Et vestro excitatae: Optata refrigeria Clientibus curate.
blocks.english: Stir up the longing of the devout, and your own; procure the desired refreshment for your clients.
blocks.editorialNote: The cited 1879 edition, p.265, visibly prints “Piorum desideria / Et vestrum excitate”. The English follows this reading as the longing of the devout and the guardians’ own longing, withdrawing the invented phrase “with your prayer”. Attached Latin remains unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Stir up their longing with your prayer, and procure the desired refreshment for your clients.

blocks.source: Vos omnes quoque coelites, In regno triumphante, Solamini hos milites, In flamma hac purgante.
blocks.english: You too, all citizens of heaven in the triumphant kingdom, comfort these soldiers amid this purifying flame.

blocks.source: Vestri in terris socii Cum fuerint laborum, Nunc et beati otii Sors vocat et bonorum.
blocks.english: Since upon earth they were your companions in labours, their lot now calls them also to blessed rest and good things.

blocks.source: O fons misericordiae, Summeque bonitatis, Prosint piorum lacrymae Hoc igne cruciatis.
blocks.english: O fountain of mercy and highest goodness, may the tears of the devout benefit those tormented in this fire.

blocks.source: Locum tuae justitiae Agnoscimus infernum, Laudes tuae clementiae Hi cantent in aeternum.
blocks.english: We acknowledge the lower world as the place of Thy justice; may these souls sing the praises of Thy mercy for ever.

blocks.source: Quot usquam estis Numini Et superis devoti, Audite quid rogemini, Ut sitis Dei toti:
blocks.english: All of you, wherever you are, devoted to God and to heaven’s citizens, hear what is asked of you, that you may belong wholly to God:

blocks.source: Haec charitatis viscera Fraternae explicate: Vices rependet misera Haec turba liberata. Amen.
blocks.english: Open your hearts in this brotherly charity; this wretched multitude, when freed, will repay you in return. Amen.
